facts.fact: The scheme is PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi), launched on 1 June 2020, giving collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors
facts.quote: The Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme, launched on 1 June 2020 to provide collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors

facts.fact: It is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (jointly with the Department of Financial Services)
facts.quote: Implementation of the scheme would be the joint responsibility of Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Department of Financial Services (DFS)

facts.fact: The Cabinet approved its restructuring on 27-08-2025 (27 August 2025) and lending is extended until 31 March 2030
facts.quote: Approved by the Union Cabinet on 27 August 2025, the lending under the restructured Scheme has been extended up to 31 March 2030

facts.fact: The loans are collateral-free working-capital term loans in three tranches
facts.quote: SVs will be eligible for collateral free working capital term loan in three tranches:

facts.fact: The 1st tranche rose to Rs 15,000 (from Rs 10,000) and the 2nd to Rs 25,000 (from Rs 20,000); the 3rd stays Rs 50,000
facts.quote: The enhanced loan structure includes first tranche loans increased up to ₹15,000 (from ₹10,000) and second tranche loans increased up to ₹25,000 (from ₹20,000), while the third tranche remains unchanged at ₹50,000.

facts.fact: Each next tranche is available on timely or early repayment of the previous one
facts.quote: Upon timely or early repayment of a tranche, vendors will be eligible for the next tranche of working capital term loans, with the enhanced limit.

facts.fact: Borrowers get an interest subsidy of 7% a year (on timely/early repayment)
facts.quote: The vendors, availing loan under the scheme, are eligible to get an interest subsidy at 7% per annum.
facts.note: The restructured scheme guidelines (MoHUA, Jan 2026) now state the 7% rate, so it no longer rests only on the 2020 portal FAQ.

facts.fact: Lenders get credit-guarantee cover through CGTMSE
facts.quote: The Scheme has a provision of Graded Guarantee Cover provided to Lending Institutions for the loans sanctioned, as indicated below, to be administered by Credit Guarantee Fund Trust

facts.fact: A UPI-linked RuPay credit card is available to vendors who have repaid the 2nd tranche
facts.quote: A UPI linked RuPay Credit Card will be available as an additional facility for PM SVANidhi beneficiaries who have successfully repaid their 2nd tranche loan and are eligible for 3rd

facts.fact: The credit card limit is up to Rs 30,000, with the operating limit starting at Rs 10,000
facts.quote: The PM SVANidhi credit card will have a credit limit of ₹30,000 (Rupees Thirty thousand). However, the operating limit will be initially fixed at ₹10,000 which

facts.fact: Digital-transaction cashback of up to Rs 1,600
facts.quote: the street vendors can avail cashback incentives upto ₹1,600 on making retail & wholesale transactions.

facts.fact: Coverage now extends to census towns and peri-urban areas in a graded manner
facts.quote: The scheme’s coverage is being expanded beyond statutory towns to census towns, peri-urban areas etc. in graded manner.

facts.fact: The scheme applies in States/UTs that have notified rules and a scheme under the Street Vendors Act, 2014
facts.quote: The scheme is available for beneficiaries belonging to only those States/UTs which have notified rules and scheme under Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

facts.fact: Apply online on pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in; the mobile number must be linked to Aadhaar
facts.quote: 2 Apply Online 2. Make sure your mobile number is linked to your Aadhaar

facts.fact: Vendors can also apply with help from a bank correspondent / MFI agent (the ULB has the list)
facts.quote: You can approach a Banking Correspondent (BC)/ Agent of Micro Finance Institution (MFI) in your area (ULBs will have the list of these persons).
facts.note: Supports 'or through the ULB/bank': the portal FAQ (2020) names bank correspondents/MFI agents, with ULBs keeping the list; the 2026 guidelines say ULBs issue the Letter of Recommendation.

summary: All claims confirmed: PIB (27 Aug 2025, 27 Aug 2026), the Jan 2026 MoHUA scheme guidelines (which now state the 7% interest subsidy), the credit card guidelines and the portal.
